# Product Vision — [Product Name]

> **Type:** Living one-page document. Date the last revision in the header — no version baselining or archive ceremony.
> **Last revised:** YYYY-MM-DD
> **Owner:** BA
> **Profile applicability:** Agile (Fixed-Range, Capacity-Based) — Vision is not produced for Waterfall projects.
> **Audience:** Client, BA, PM, delivery team.
> **Update frequency:** Stable. Updated only at major direction changes (new market, new persona, big pivot).
> **Confluence:** [URL — pending]

---

## 1. Why This Product Exists

[One paragraph. The underlying business or customer problem the product is solving, and what makes it worth doing now. Plain language; no implementation detail. This is the answer to *"why are we building this?"* — the North Star paragraph the team should be able to recite.]

---

## 2. Who It's For

**Primary users:** [user group; one-line description — who they are, what they do, where they sit in the customer's organisation]
**Secondary users:** [user group, if any — typically a related role who interacts with the product indirectly]
**Indirect stakeholders:** [client leadership, end-customers of the customer, or others whose outcomes are affected]

---

## 3. What Problem It Solves

[Two or three sentences: the current-state pain in concrete terms, and the change the product produces. Avoid feature lists — describe the *outcome*, not the *mechanism*.]

---

## 4. What Success Looks Like

[Three to five directional indicators of success. These are *outcome* statements, not Roadmap metrics — the Roadmap will set targets and dates. The Vision sets the shape of "good".]

- [Indicator 1]
- [Indicator 2]
- [Indicator 3]
- [Indicator 4]
- [Indicator 5]

---

## 5. Why Us / Why Now

[One paragraph on competitive position, market timing, and capability fit. Why is this the product to build, by this team, on this timeline? Not a sales pitch — a strategic rationale that frames future Roadmap priority calls.]

---

## 6. What This Product Is Not

[Two to four explicit anti-statements. Out-of-scope at the *strategic* level — distinct from the Charter's tactical scope boundary. These statements anchor future scope conversations: when someone proposes feature X, this section is the answer to *"is X consistent with the Vision?"*.]

- Not [strategic anti-statement 1]
- Not [strategic anti-statement 2]
- Not [strategic anti-statement 3]
